claims.text: The starting material is an equimolar bulk HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy.
A specimen containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen resembles typical experimental HfNbTaTiZr specimens.
HfNbTaTiZr contains realistic atomic-scale chemical disorder relevant to thermal transport.
A DFT-calibrated interatomic-potential framework is suitable for atomistic modeling of a high-entropy alloy.
Combining machine-learned interatomic potentials with anharmonic lattice dynamics can independently calculate phonon lifetimes in HfNbTaTiZr.
Time-dependent perturbation theory can independently calculate electronic scattering rates in HfNbTaTiZr.
Atomic-scale disorder produces distinct phonon-scattering events in HfNbTaTiZr.
Approximately 1 wt.% oxygen produces impurity scattering of phonons in HfNbTaTiZr.
Atomic-scale disorder and approximately 1 wt.% oxygen produce electron-scattering events in HfNbTaTiZr.
Independent calculations of anharmonic phonon lifetimes and electronic scattering rates allow lattice and electronic thermal conductivity to be separated.
Earlier Debye- or DFT-elastic-based thermal-conductivity approaches assume ideal, defect-free crystals.
Earlier Debye- or DFT-elastic-based approaches typically conflate phononic and electronic heat transport.
Explicit treatment of atomic disorder and oxygen impurity scattering will outperform earlier Debye- or DFT-elastic-based approaches.
The proposed framework will reduce predictive error by approximately 30–50% relative to earlier simplified approaches.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr will be nearly equal.
From 300 to 1200 K, HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen will have total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m).
The method is applicable only under steady-state conditions without phase transitions or non-equilibrium defect dynamics.
The predicted error and carrier separation are sensitive to disorder level, impurity concentration, and simulation parameters.
